summary: Space Junior is a browser-based educational game inspired by NASA’s Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) program. Players take on the role of a mission commander in a stylized, isometric Martian habitat inspired by Mars Dune Alpha. They coordinate a four-person crew—including a medical officer, a science officer, and a flight engineer—and make decisions about limited resources, crew well-being, habitat maintenance, and food production. Through short scenarios and visible consequences, Space Junior introduces younger audiences to the practical challenges of preparing for long-duration space exploration.
details:
The problem

Space exploration is exciting, but its less visible challenges are difficult for many young learners to imagine: a crew must balance life support, power, health, scientific work, maintenance, and food production while operating far from Earth. Traditional explanations of these topics can feel abstract. We want to make them easier to understand through decisions that students can explore for themselves.

Our solution

Space Junior presents a low-poly, isometric environment inspired by the Mars Dune Alpha habitat used in NASA’s CHAPEA analog missions. The player serves as commander of a four-member team. The other crew positions—medical officer, science officer, and flight engineer—are represented as in-game characters, enabling task-based interactions and team coordination.

How the game works

Explore the habitat and recognize its functional areas, including areas related to living, research, maintenance, and food production.

Monitor key game indicators such as energy, life support, shielding, and crew condition.

Review mission objectives and decide how to prioritize limited supplies and crew tasks.

Respond to short dilemmas, such as whether to allocate energy to the greenhouse when other systems also need power.

Experience a simulated space-weather alert and prepare the base using the resources available in the game.

Reflect on the trade-offs between immediate mission needs and long-term crew survival.

Current prototype and scope

The current prototype visually represents an isometric habitat with rooms, solar panels, an astronaut character, mission indicators, and a crew decision prompt. The intended learning experience includes crew coordination, resource management, and mission scenarios. Any additional mechanics should be described as completed only after they are implemented and tested.

Educational value

The game is designed to encourage systems thinking, planning, teamwork, and scientific curiosity. Players see that an apparently simple choice—such as saving energy—can have consequences elsewhere in the habitat. Instead of only memorizing facts about Mars missions, they practice evaluating competing priorities.

Technologies and design

Space Junior is a browser-based interactive prototype with a stylized low-poly 3D visual direction and an isometric camera.

Space Junior was built with TypeScript, React, HTML, and CSS. Its 3D environment uses Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei. Vite handles development and production builds, while Node.js and npm support the tooling and tests. Python scripts retrieve and prepare historical NASA data, which is stored locally in JSON files. The project uses GitHub Actions for automated builds and deployment to GitHub Pages.

What makes it different

Space Junior connects a friendly game presentation with a documented NASA analog program. Its main contribution is not a new spaceflight prediction model; it is a learning experience that makes the operational trade-offs of a four-person Mars analog crew understandable to a broader audience.
